cards.label: Set program goals in measurable terms, such as peak wet weather flow reduction per basin and a target share of private side sources addressed

Divide the city into study basins using trunk sewers, lift station catchments, and natural drainage boundaries that can each be flow monitored

tasks.explanation: Both options must be priced against the same peak flow and service level or the comparison is meaningless. A sensitivity case protects the decision, because removal programs rarely perform exactly as first estimated.

tasks.prompt: Order a private side I/I source removal program for residential areas.

Pilot the program on one neighbourhood block group and measure participation rates, defects found, and cost per property corrected
Confirm the private side share of wet weather flow from basin data so the program size matches the source, not a guess
Arrange contractor capacity and inspection staff for the repair volume the pilot predicts before expanding the offer citywide
Measure wet weather flow in the completed basins against the pre program baseline and report the removal achieved
Design the program offer, including inspection method, who pays for each repair type, permits, and how work on private property is authorized

tasks.explanation: Private side work succeeds on participation, so the pilot tests the offer before the city commits. Phased expansion matched to contractor capacity avoids a backlog of approved but unfinished repairs.

tasks.prompt: Order a manhole rehabilitation program aimed at infiltration reduction.

Group the defects by repair method, such as cover replacement, frame seals, chimney liners, and full structure rehabilitation
Package the repairs into contracts by basin so a whole basin can be remeasured after its structures are sealed
Inspect manholes in the priority basins during and after wet weather and grade each for frame and cover inflow, chimney leakage, and wall and benching defects
Rank the work by infiltration removed per structure and by flood risk at each location, not by age alone
Complete the first basin package and hold quality checks on seals and liners before the next package is released

tasks.explanation: Manhole inflow is removed basin by basin so the effect can be metered, not assumed. Grouping by repair method makes efficient contracts, and remeasurement closes the loop on whether sealing worked.

tasks.prompt: Order the long term effectiveness review of a five year I/I program.

tasks.configuration: Scope: the program has completed source removal in four basins, and management needs to know whether the promised peak flow reduction arrived.

cards.label: Compare wet weather response for storms of similar size and antecedent conditions so the comparison is fair
Assemble the pre program baseline flows, the storm records, and the completed source removal inventory for each finished basin
Identify basins where removal underperformed and diagnose whether sources remain, repairs failed, or the original estimate was optimistic
Report effectiveness by basin with cost per unit of peak flow removed and recommend where the next program phase should focus
Separate the flow change explained by completed removals from changes due to growth, new connections, and drier or wetter weather
Remeter each finished basin over a wet season with rain gauges placed as they were for the baseline study

tasks.explanation: Effectiveness can only be judged against storms of similar size, which is why the baseline method is repeated exactly. Separating growth and weather from removal keeps the verdict honest and points the next phase at real remaining sources.

tasks.prompt: Order a smoke testing program to find direct inflow connections in an older district.

cards.label: Notify residents, the fire dispatch centre, and affected businesses in writing before testing, with dates and what smoke at a property means
Blow smoke through the section and record every emergence point with photos, addresses, and an estimate of the opening size
Issue correction notices for confirmed connections and enter all findings in the basin source inventory with reinspection dates
Brief crews on properties to watch, including roof leaders, area drains, cleanouts, and buildings where smoke indoors must be reported at once
Isolate the test section between manholes, confirm the blower setup, and check weather so smoke behaviour will be readable
Follow up the strongest inflow points with dye testing or property visits to confirm the connection before any correction notice is issued

tasks.explanation: Notification comes first because smoke in a home alarms people and the fire service. Confirmation before a correction notice protects owners from being ordered to fix a connection that was never proven.

tasks.prompt: Order a groundwater infiltration reduction plan for sewers below the water table.

cards.label: Schedule the sealing work for the season when access and curing conditions suit the method, with flow control planned for live sewers
Verify by night flow measurement after the work in the next high groundwater season and record the base flow change
Inspect the suspect reaches by CCTV at high groundwater and record joint leakage, crack weeping, and lateral connection leakage by severity
Confirm the infiltration reaches by comparing dry weather flows in high and low groundwater seasons and by night flow analysis
Select the method per reach, such as joint grouting, cured in place lining, or open cut renewal, using condition and access
Rank reaches by infiltration volume per metre and by structural condition, since leaking but sound pipe suits sealing while failed pipe suits renewal

tasks.explanation: Infiltration through joints follows the groundwater season, so both the inspection and the proof are timed to high water. Method follows condition, because grouting a structurally failed pipe wastes the sealing investment.

tasks.prompt: Order the integration of I/I findings into the sewer rehabilitation capital plan.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. cards.label: Merge the I/I list with the structural rehabilitation list and flag reaches where one project can solve both problems at once
Sequence projects so upstream source removal precedes downstream capacity decisions that depend on the reduced flow
Consolidate the basin study findings into one ranked source list with flows, locations, and removal methods for the whole city
Update the plan each year with completed work, remeasured flows, and new study results rather than treating it as fixed
Estimate each combined project with given unit rates and the flow and risk reduction it delivers
Present the ten year plan with annual spending, expected peak flow trend, and the projects deferred with their residual risk stated

tasks.explanation: I/I and structural work planned together avoid lining a pipe and then digging it for capacity. Sequencing removal before capacity decisions is what turns study findings into avoided capital cost.

tasks.prompt: Order a foundation drain disconnection study for a neighbourhood with chronic wet weather surcharging.

tasks.configuration: Scope: the neighbourhood predates current practice, many homes connect foundation drains to the sanitary sewer, and surcharging occurs in large storms.

cards.label: Design a disconnection approach with the plumbing and permit requirements, owner costs, and any city assistance defined
Decide on the wider program, including whether it stays voluntary or becomes required at property sale or renovation, and report the flow evidence
Check where disconnected water can go, including storm sewer capacity, lot grading, and winter icing risk for surface discharges
Survey a sample of homes with owner permission to confirm connection patterns and where a sump pump and discharge could be installed
Estimate the foundation drain contribution from storm flow response, home age and type, and any existing sump pump records for the area
Run a voluntary pilot on one street, monitor its storm response, and record owner experience and actual installation costs

tasks.explanation: Disconnection moves water rather than deleting it, so the receiving route and winter icing are checked before any home is changed. The pilot proves both the flow benefit and the owner experience before policy is set.

tasks.prompt: Order the long term cold climate adaptation review for collection infrastructure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: freeze thaw cycles are increasing, frost depths are changing, and the utility reviews its design and maintenance standards for the next 25 years.

cards.label: Propose standard changes and program adjustments in order of the risk they retire, using given rates where costs are compared
Adopt the proven changes into the design manual with a review cycle, since the climate input will continue to move
Identify the asset groups most exposed, including shallow services, older clay sewers in frost susceptible soils, and exposed station components
Compare current design standards, such as burial depth, insulation practice, and station cold provisions, with the conditions the records now show
Gather the evidence of change from the utility records, including freeze incidents, frost related breaks, thaw inflow trends, and winter access problems
Pilot the most consequential standard change on the next suitable projects and monitor the results against the old standard

tasks.explanation: Adaptation grounded in the utility own freeze and break records survives scrutiny that generic climate claims do not. Piloting the biggest standard change before adopting it everywhere keeps a 25 year decision honest.

tasks.prompt: Order the building of a ten year sewer rehabilitation program from condition data.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: the city holds graded CCTV data for 60 percent of its sewers and must set a defensible renewal program.

cards.label: Group triggered reaches into project packages by basin and street so excavation, traffic, and lining work are done once per area
Publish the program with the backlog trend it produces, so management sees whether the renewal rate is gaining on deterioration
Consolidate condition grades, age, material, failure history, and consequence data into one asset register view for every sewer reach
Sequence packages by risk so the highest likelihood and consequence combinations are renewed first across the ten years
Define the renewal triggers, such as the worst structural grades, repeated failures, and reaches where failure consequence is unacceptable at any grade
Estimate package costs with given unit rates and set the annual program size the budget and contractor market can actually deliver

tasks.explanation: A program built on triggers and risk can be defended line by line. Publishing the backlog trend is the honesty check, because a renewal rate below the deterioration rate is a growing problem, not a plan.

tasks.prompt: Order the selection between lining, pipe bursting, and open cut renewal for a project area.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: one project area has 2 km of deteriorated sewer with mixed diameters, several sags, and two reaches needing larger capacity.

cards.label: Check lateral connections and their condition in each reach, because the renewal method must restore every live service
List the hard constraints for the area, including reaches needing upsizing, sags needing grade correction, and access or surface limits on excavation
Carry the chosen methods into design with the pre renewal cleaning and CCTV requirements each method needs
Screen out methods that cannot meet the constraints, since lining cannot fix grade or add much capacity and bursting needs suitable soil and separation
Assign the method per reach and record the reason, so a mixed method project is a decision, not an accident
Compare the surviving methods reach by reach on given unit rates, service life, disruption, and risk during construction

tasks.explanation: Constraints eliminate methods before cost is compared, which prevents choosing a liner for a pipe whose real problem is grade. Recording the reason per reach lets design proceed without reopening settled questions.

tasks.prompt: Order a cured in place lining program for a year of scattered sewer reaches.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: 3.5 km of lining is planned across 14 reaches, all in live residential streets with active services.

cards.label: Verify every live lateral in each reach from records and dye or camera checks so reinstatement after lining is complete
Supervise installation and curing records, collect liner samples as specified, and hold acceptance until post lining CCTV is reviewed
Sequence the reaches into installation days by diameter and access, with bypass pumping plans sized for peak flow in each reach
Enter accepted reaches into the asset register with new condition grade, liner details, and the warranty expiry date
Confirm each reach with recent CCTV, cleaning records, and measured dimensions so liner thickness and length are ordered correctly
Notify affected residents of the work dates, the water use restrictions during cure, and the contact for odour or backup concerns

tasks.explanation: Lining quality is decided before the resin arrives, by measurement, lateral verification, and bypass capacity. Acceptance on post lining CCTV and cure records, not on installation alone, is what starts the warranty honestly.

tasks.prompt: Order a lateral rehabilitation program for a district with root and infiltration problems at services.

cards.label: Verify each finished lateral by camera and record the seal or liner installed in the property and asset files
Set the cost sharing and access rules with property owners in writing before any lateral is scheduled
Rank laterals by defect evidence from launch camera surveys, backup history, and the infiltration measured at the district meter
Schedule lateral work street by street with the connection seals done while access and bypass arrangements are in place
Remeter the district after the first streets are complete and adjust the program scope if the flow response differs from the estimate
Define the rehabilitation scope per lateral, from connection sealing at the main to full lateral lining to the property line

tasks.explanation: After mainline renewal, laterals often dominate the remaining infiltration, so the program follows the meter. Written cost sharing before scheduling prevents the disputes that stall private side work.

tasks.prompt: Order a spot repair program for isolated structural defects found by CCTV.

Group defects by repair method, such as robotic grouting, internal patch liners, and short open cut repairs where internal methods cannot reach
Schedule internal repairs in batches by area to share traffic control, bypass, and camera crew costs across nearby defects
Confirm each defect from the graded CCTV record with chainage, clock position, and a check that the surrounding pipe is truly sound
Rank the groups by failure risk and by whether the defect is actively leaking soil or groundwater into the pipe
Verify each repair by CCTV after completion and grade the repaired location before the work is accepted

tasks.explanation: Spot repair only pays when the surrounding pipe is genuinely sound, which the record check proves first. Batching by area shares the fixed costs, and post repair grading keeps the condition data truthful.

tasks.prompt: Order the rehabilitation design review for a trunk sewer renewal project.

Review the design basis, including the design flows, the condition evidence, and the service life the renewal is required to deliver
Record review comments as accepted, rejected with reason, or requiring redesign, and confirm the designer responds to each before tender
Approve the design for tender only when the flow, access, and restoration checks are closed, and file the review in the project record
Verify the design restores every connection and manhole in the reach and addresses the manhole defects found in the condition survey
Check the bypass and flow management design against peak wet weather flow, not average flow, with a contingency for a storm during construction

tasks.prompt: Order a rehabilitation pilot project to test a new renewal method before program adoption.

Carry out the pilot with the supplier present but city inspection recording production, problems, and actual quantities used
Decide adoption, limited adoption, or rejection in a written report that other project teams can rely on
Set the acceptance criteria in advance, covering leakage reduction, finish quality, production rate, and unit cost from given rates
Measure the baseline carefully, including CCTV grading, joint leakage evidence, and night flow in the pilot reach
Remeasure the pilot reaches after a groundwater season and compare results against the criteria set before the work

tasks.prompt: Order the prioritization workshop that ranks rehabilitation projects for the annual budget.

tasks.configuration: Scope: project requests exceed the budget by three times, and operations, engineering, and finance staff must produce one ranked list.

cards.label: Confirm the funded list, the deferred list with its stated risks, and the projects that need more condition data before they can compete
Minute the decisions and owners, and feed the deferred risks into the risk register and next year CCTV priorities
Require each project submission to carry its condition evidence, failure history, and cost estimate on the same one page format
Issue the scoring criteria in advance, covering failure likelihood, consequence, regulatory and overflow risk, and coordination with road work
Test the draft ranking by asking what failure the city accepts for each project pushed below the funding line
Score the projects in the workshop against the criteria, with disagreements recorded rather than averaged away

tasks.explanation: Common criteria and one page evidence make projects comparable instead of loudest first. Naming the failure accepted for each deferred project turns a budget line into an honest risk decision.

tasks.prompt: Order the renewal program coordination with the city road reconstruction program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Agree the shared schedule, cost splits for shared excavation and restoration, and who leads each combined project
Overlay the sewer renewal priorities on the road program map and list every street where both programs need the same pavement
Review the overlay annually, because road priorities shift and a missed street becomes an emergency cut in new pavement
For streets reconstructed before sewer renewal is due, confirm the sewer condition is good enough to outlast the moratorium period
Track the combined projects in both programs with the same milestones so a slip in one is visible to the other

tasks.explanation: The overlay is simple and saves the most money of any coordination step. Checking that sewers under soon to be rebuilt roads can outlast the moratorium prevents the emergency cut everyone is trying to avoid.

tasks.prompt: Order the post project review of a completed rehabilitation contract.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Close the contract only when warranty start dates, holdback release conditions, and outstanding items are documented and assigned
Examine the complaint record for the problem street and separate construction impacts that were unavoidable from ones caused by poor practice
Review the acceptance records, deficiency lists, and warranty items to confirm everything contracted was actually delivered and corrected
Compare the contract quantities and final cost with the estimate and identify which items drove the variance
Record lessons for estimating, specification, and supervision in the program file where the next project team will find them

tasks.explanation: A review that only checks cost misses whether the assets were delivered and recorded. Lessons filed where the next team works, not in a separate report, are the ones that change the next contract.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual CMOM program self assessment for the collection utility.

tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility runs a capacity, management, operations and maintenance program and reviews it every year before budget season.

cards.label: Identify the gaps that contributed to any overflow, backup cluster, or capacity surprise during the year
File the assessment and track the gap actions quarterly so the next annual review starts from progress, not from memory
Gather the year evidence for each program element, including overflow records, cleaning and inspection completion, and capacity study status
Present the assessment to management with the scores, the gap actions, and the measures that will show improvement
Score each element against the program document, marking elements as in place, partly in place, or missing, with evidence for each score
Convert the top gaps into funded actions with owners and dates, sized to what the next budget can carry

tasks.explanation: Scoring against evidence rather than intention is what makes a self assessment worth doing. Gap actions with owners and dates are the bridge between the review and the budget that follows it.

tasks.prompt: Order the capacity assurance review for a sewershed approaching its design flow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. cards.label: Identify the first element that limits capacity and the flow at which surcharging begins there
Assemble the flow monitoring record, growth connections added, and the I/I removal completed in the shed to date
Adopt a capacity plan with trigger flows that start design or construction early enough to be ready before the limit is reached
Project the peak wet weather flow for the approved development horizon using given growth and peaking factors
Evaluate the response options, including further I/I removal, storage, upsizing, and development phasing, on the same flow basis
Compare the projection with the capacity of each element in the path, including trunk reaches, the lift station, and the force main

tasks.explanation: Capacity assurance works on triggers set before the limit arrives, because design and construction take years. Checking every element in the path matters, since the limit is usually one reach or one station, not the whole shed.

tasks.prompt: Order the routine update of the overflow response plan under the CMOM program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. cards.label: Update contact lists, call out rosters, equipment locations, and the notification steps for the regulator and public health contacts in general terms
Revise the plan from the exercise findings, including any step that responders could not complete as written
Check the plan against current field reality, including bypass pump sizes, hose and fitting compatibility, and access at known overflow points
Issue the new version with a version date, withdraw old copies from trucks and stations, and brief all shifts on the changes
Compare the plan against the overflows of the last two years and list where responders actually departed from it and why
Run a tabletop exercise with the response crews and dispatch using a wet weather overflow scenario at a sensitive location

tasks.explanation: A plan is only true if the pumps, fittings, and phone numbers in it still exist. The tabletop exercise finds the broken steps on a quiet day instead of during a storm.

tasks.prompt: Order the monthly CMOM performance dashboard review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: the dashboard tracks overflows, backups, cleaning and CCTV completion, lift station alarms, and complaint response times.

cards.label: Record the review in the program file, including measures accepted as seasonal and the evidence for that judgement
Investigate the measures off target, assigning each a cause from the records rather than accepting the number at face value
Pull the month data from the work order, alarm, and overflow records and check it for missing or duplicated entries before the meeting
Agree corrective actions for the off target measures, with owners and the month by which the effect should show
Carry unresolved measures forward visibly on the next dashboard so they cannot quietly drop off the agenda
Compare each measure with its target and with the same month last year so seasonal effects are not mistaken for trends

tasks.explanation: Checking the data before the meeting prevents managing from recording errors. Carrying unresolved measures forward is the discipline that stops the same gap being rediscovered every quarter.

tasks.prompt: Order the legal and regulatory awareness review inside the CMOM program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: the program requires staff to know the reporting duties that apply to overflows and bypasses under provincial requirements in general terms and the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations as general references.

cards.label: Record the review and the procedure corrections in the CMOM program file with the next review date
Compare the list with the last year of actual reports and check that every reportable event was reported with complete information
Correct any procedure step where the reporting duty and the field paperwork do not match, such as missing volume estimate fields
List the events the utility must report, the information each report needs, and the time limits the procedures state in general terms
Brief supervisors and dispatch staff on the duties using the utility own recent events as teaching examples
Set a file check each quarter in which a sample of overflow files is audited for reporting completeness

tasks.explanation: Reporting failures are usually paperwork design failures, so the field forms are checked against the duty, not just the staff. Using the utility own events as examples makes the duty concrete for the people who will make the call.

tasks.prompt: Order the CMOM documentation audit for collection system records.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: an internal audit samples whether maps, inspection records, and work histories match what the program document promises.

cards.label: Classify each finding as a missing record, an inaccurate record, or a record that exists but cannot be retrieved when needed
Define the sample, covering map accuracy for new subdivisions, CCTV record completeness, and work order closure quality across districts
Set the retrieval test, in which a duty operator must find a named record within a set time, and repeat it after corrections
Report the audit results and the correction status to management and schedule the next sample before the findings go stale
Assign corrections with owners, starting with records that affect emergency response and capacity decisions
Check sampled records against field or source evidence, such as as built drawings and contractor deliveries, rather than against other records only

tasks.explanation: Records that cannot be retrieved during an event are functionally missing, which is why the audit ends with a timed retrieval test. Correcting emergency and capacity records first puts the effort where bad data does the most harm.

tasks.prompt: Order the sewer use and source control element review within the CMOM program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. tasks.configuration: Scope: the element covers fats, oils and grease control, hauled waste receiving, and prohibited discharge follow up for the collection system.

Confirm the hauled waste receiving procedure records source, volume, and load character for every load accepted
Report element performance with the cleaning program results so source control and cleaning are judged together
Compare blockage locations with inspection status and target the next inspection round at premises upstream of repeat blockages
Check inspection coverage of food service premises against the inventory so uninspected premises are visible, not assumed compliant
Update the element procedures where records show a step is skipped in practice, and brief the inspectors on the change

tasks.explanation: Source control and cleaning are two halves of the same grease problem, so they are reported together. Targeting inspections upstream of repeat blockages spends inspector time where the evidence points.

tasks.prompt: Order the customer complaint and basement backup tracking routine under CMOM.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: backup complaints arrive through the city call centre, field crews, and an after hours line, and the records do not yet agree with each other.

cards.label: Feed clusters into the cleaning, CCTV, and capacity programs as work, with the originating complaint references attached
Report monthly counts by cause and cluster so management sees whether field programs are reducing repeat events at the same addresses
Classify each event by the cause found in the field, separating mainline problems, lateral problems, and plumbing problems inside the home
Merge the three intake sources into one register with duplicates removed and each event tied to an address and a work order
Check response times and the information given to residents against the program standard for backup events
Map the classified events and identify clusters that indicate a mainline capacity or condition problem rather than isolated laterals

tasks.explanation: Three intake lists that disagree hide repeat addresses, which are the strongest signal of a mainline problem. Classification by cause found, not by first impression, keeps lateral problems from inflating the mainline program and the reverse.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual training and competency review for collection staff under CMOM.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the review covers operators, crew leaders, and supervisors across cleaning, CCTV, lift stations, and emergency response duties.

cards.label: Compare the training records with the role requirements and list every expired or missing item by person and crew
Schedule the missing training and observations into the work calendar so crews are not pulled from emergency coverage to complete them
List the competencies each role requires from the program document, including safety certifications and equipment authorizations
File the review with completion tracking and set the mid year check for items that were scheduled but not delivered
Check field competency by sampling supervised task observations for the highest risk duties, such as confined space entry and bypass pumping
Brief supervisors on coaching points from the observations, such as steps crews perform differently from the written procedure

tasks.explanation: Records alone overstate competency, so high risk duties are also observed in the field. Differences between crew practice and the written procedure are treated as information about both, not automatically as crew error.

tasks.prompt: Order the CMOM program budget justification package for the coming year.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the package must link every requested dollar to a program element and a measurable result from the current year.

cards.label: Offer a reduced funding scenario that names the work that would not be done and the risk accepted with it
Record the approved funding against each element so next year results can be compared with what was actually resourced
Build each request with the work volume, the given unit rate, and the result the volume is expected to produce
Identify the service risks that grow if funding stays flat, stated as specific assets and sheds rather than general warnings
Start from the current year results, listing what each element delivered, such as metres cleaned, overflows by cause, and capacity studies completed
Present the package to management with the dashboard trends attached so the numbers in the room match the program record

tasks.explanation: Linking money to delivered results is what separates a program budget from a wish list. The reduced scenario forces an explicit risk decision instead of a silent cut that surfaces later as an overflow.

tasks.prompt: Order the building of a collection asset register from maps and field records.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the utility is replacing a map only inventory with a register that carries age, material, condition, and criticality for every asset.

cards.label: Field verify a sample in each district, including manholes shown on maps that cannot be found and assets found that are not mapped
Publish the register with a data confidence note per asset group so planners know which decisions the data can support
Define the asset hierarchy first, from system down through sheds, reaches, manholes, stations, and components, so every record has one place
Load condition grades from CCTV and station assessments and set the rule for how grades age when no new inspection occurs
Load the base inventory from the mapping system and reconcile counts against as built records and the station equipment lists
Attach the known attributes, age, material, size, and depth, and mark attributes that are estimated rather than recorded

tasks.explanation: A hierarchy agreed first prevents the register becoming a pile of disconnected lists. Marking estimated attributes as estimated protects planners from treating guesses as survey facts.

tasks.prompt: Order a criticality assessment for collection system assets.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: criticality will drive inspection frequency and spares, covering trunk sewers, river crossings, lift stations, and force mains.

cards.label: Check the top band in the field or from records to confirm no asset is critical only because of a data error
Define consequence categories with management, including environmental harm at watercourse crossings, basement flooding, road and rail disruption, and repair difficulty
Review the bands annually and after any major failure, since a single event can rewrite the likelihood evidence
Score consequence for each asset group using location, depth, size, and what lies above and downstream of the asset
Set the inspection frequency, monitoring, and spares that each band receives, and record the cost of that service level
Combine consequence with likelihood from condition and failure history to place each asset in a criticality band

tasks.explanation: Criticality is consequence times likelihood, and both halves need evidence. Field checking the top band matters because inspection budgets will follow those scores for years.

tasks.prompt: Order the lifecycle cost comparison for a lift station renewal decision.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a 30 year old station needs either a major rehabilitation or a full replacement, and management wants the whole life comparison using given rates.

cards.label: Cost each option over the same horizon using given rates for capital, energy, maintenance, and the mid life component renewals each will need
Recommend the option with the lower whole life cost that still meets the capacity and reliability requirements, naming any non cost reason to choose otherwise
Add the risk cost difference, such as the expected overflow and emergency repair exposure of the older structure if it is retained
Record the decision and its assumptions in the asset file so a future review can see why replacement was or was not chosen
Define the options precisely, including the scope, capacity, and service life each option actually delivers
State the assumptions that most affect the answer, especially energy price, service life, and discount treatment directed by finance

tasks.explanation: Options compared over different lives or capacities produce a confident wrong answer. Recording assumptions in the asset file lets a future reviewer test the decision instead of relitigating it from memory.

tasks.prompt: Order the annual asset condition summary that feeds the capital plan.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the summary covers sewers, manholes, and stations and must show how much of the network sits in each condition band.

cards.label: Present the summary with the renewal rate needed to hold the backlog steady, stated plainly beside the funded rate
Identify districts where condition data is too old to trust and assign CCTV or inspection work to refresh them before they drive capital decisions
Extract condition grades by asset group and age band from the register and check the share of assets with no current grade
Translate the worst band assets into candidate projects with given unit rates and group them by area for the capital planners
File the summary as the dated baseline the next year summary will be compared against
Calculate the value and length in the worst two bands and compare with last year to show whether the backlog is growing or shrinking

tasks.explanation: The share of assets with no grade is reported beside the grades themselves, because unknown condition is a finding. Comparing the funded renewal rate with the rate needed to hold the backlog steady is the summary core message.

tasks.prompt: Order a spare parts criticality review for the lift station fleet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: stores holds parts for 22 stations, some shelves hold parts for retired pumps, and two recent events waited days for components.

cards.label: Review the list after every major failure and annually, adding any component whose absence extended an outage
Check current stock against that list and flag critical items with no spare, long lead time, or a spare that fits only one station
Set minimum stock for the critical list from lead time and failure frequency, and arrange shared spares where stations use identical equipment
List station components whose failure stops the station or removes its backup, using the failure records and station designs
Remove or return parts for equipment no longer in service and record the disposal so the catalogue stays truthful
Fund the gaps in order of station criticality and record expected delivery dates for long lead items

tasks.explanation: Spares earn their shelf by the outage they prevent, so the review starts from failure consequence. Deleting parts for retired equipment matters because a catalogue that lies about what is available is worse than a short list.

tasks.prompt: Order the asset data update routine after a capital project is completed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: three renewal projects closed this quarter and the register, maps, and condition grades must reflect the new assets before the next planning cycle.

cards.label: Reset the age, material, and condition fields for renewed assets and attach the project reference and warranty expiry
Collect the as built drawings, acceptance CCTV, liner and material records, and warranty documents from each project file
Notify the planning, operations, and finance users that the update is live and which reports now use the new data
Sample check the updated records against the as builts and log any project whose documentation is still incomplete with an owner to chase it
Reconcile the project asset list against the register so no renewed reach keeps its old failing grade into the next ranking
Update the mapping with the new alignments, sizes, and manhole locations and retire the records of assets removed from service

tasks.explanation: Renewed assets that keep old grades get renewed twice on paper and distort every ranking. The sample check closes the loop, because documentation promised at project close often arrives late or not at all.

tasks.prompt: Order a risk based inspection plan for river and rail crossings.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the city has 14 watercourse crossings and 5 rail crossings, several are siphons or aerial crossings that cannot be inspected by standard CCTV alone.

cards.label: Inventory the crossings with their type, access, isolation options, and the consequence of failure at each location
Sequence the plan so unknown condition at high consequence crossings is resolved first, even where access makes the work expensive
Set the reinspection interval per crossing from the condition found and add any needed repair to the rehabilitation program with its risk stated
Select the inspection method per crossing, such as sonar, laser profiling, diver or drawdown inspection, based on type and flow
Review the inspection history and the last known condition, and list crossings where condition is effectively unknown
Carry out the inspections with the isolation and environmental precautions each site requires and record condition in the register

tasks.explanation: Crossings concentrate consequence, so unknown condition there outranks easy inspections elsewhere. Method follows crossing type, because a siphon surveyed with the wrong tool produces a report and no knowledge.

tasks.prompt: Order the level of service review for the collection utility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: council wants stated service levels for overflows, backups, odour response, and new development capacity, with the cost of each level shown.

cards.label: Record the adopted levels in the asset management plan and align the CMOM targets and dashboard measures with them
Review performance against the adopted levels annually and report shortfalls with the cause, whether funding, capacity, or delivery
Measure current performance against each candidate level from the program records and identify where the utility already complies or falls short
Draft candidate service levels in measurable terms, such as response times, inspection coverage, and the storm size the system should carry without surcharging
Present the levels with their costs and the residual risk at each, so the choice is made with its price attached
Cost the work required to hold each level using given unit rates, including the capital projects the higher levels would force

tasks.explanation: A service level without its cost is a slogan. Aligning the dashboard with the adopted levels afterwards is what turns a council decision into daily management information.

tasks.prompt: Order the deterioration forecast for the sewer network renewal budget.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 3 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations and the CCME Canada-wide Strategy as general references, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: finance asks how the renewal backlog will move over 20 years at three funding levels, using the register condition and age data.

cards.label: Project how much length enters the worst condition bands in each five year period if no renewal occurs
Check the forecast against the last five years of actual condition movement and adjust the patterns where the utility data disagrees
Group the network by material and age and assign each group a deterioration pattern from the utility own condition history where it exists
Record the forecast assumptions in the plan so the next update can test them against new condition data
Apply each funding level as a renewal volume per year and project the backlog and the worst band share over the horizon
Present the three futures with the risk each carries, including the point where emergency repairs begin to dominate spending

tasks.explanation: A forecast checked against the utility own recent condition movement beats a generic curve. Showing when emergency work begins to dominate makes the cost of underfunding visible in operational terms, not just dollars.
